ranked_facts.why: The presence of a milky white layer on the surface of the blood sample, indicative of hypertriglyceridemia, is more characteristic of lipoprotein lipase deficiency, a type of lipid storage disease, than glycogen storage disease.
Hypertriglyceridemia causing lactescent plasma is a hallmark of lipoprotein lipase deficiency, which is a lipid storage disease, and is not typically seen in glycogen storage diseases.
